newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X active after Busang report.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X active after Busang report.

text.p: Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd traded heavily in Toronto on Friday after an Indonesian newspaper reported that partner Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc may pull out of the Busang gold project.
Bre-X stock was unchanged at 3.60 in turnover of 2.5 million shares, topping actives on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
In New York, Freeport shares were off 3/8 at 28-1/2 in light trading.

Harian Ekonomi Neraca newspaper said in a report on Friday that New Orleans-based Freeport was planning to withdraw officially from the project before results of an independent audit of Busang were announced.
Last month, Freeport reported finding "insignificant amounts" of gold from preliminary tests of Busang, casting doubt on potentially the century's biggest gold find.
Freeport said earlier this week that continued testing of its original drill cores had still not found significant gold.
Bre-X has hired Toronto-based Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd to conduct an audit of its Busang project. The results are expected as a early as next week.

"At best, this way Freeport can avoid any possible (legal) suit that may arise," the Neraca newspaper quoted an anonymous source as saying. "And this (suit) is quite possible," the source told the newspaper.
The Neraca newspaper also quoted a spokeswoman for a consortium of Indonesian Busang partners as denying Freeport would withdraw from the project.
"The rumors are not true. The share ownership composition has not changed," Nia Sarinastiti was quoted as saying.
Freeport spokeswoman Kristin Lemkau said on Friday the firm had no comment beyond its earlier statements on Busang.
"We're not going to comment. We will elect to participate only if the development is economically feasible," she said in a telephone interview.
Lemkau declined to comment on whether Freeport would wait to make its decision on Busang until after the Strathcona report was released.
Bre-X has a 45 percent stake in Busang, Freeport has 15 percent, the Indonesian government 10 percent and local companies the remaining 30 percent.
